target.title: fix(aws): bootstrap SSH over Tailscale hostname when enabled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `--network tailscale` on the AWS provider, bootstrap readiness probes
and SSH targets always used the instance public IPv4. When the crabbox
operator runs on EC2 in the same account/region, AWS drops EC2→EC2
public-IP traffic without VPC peering. The leased box joins the tailnet
via cloud-init and is reachable there, but `warmup` hangs on the public
IP probe until timeout.

## Evidence

```console
$ go test ./internal/providers/aws/ -count=1 -run TestBootstrapSSHHost
ok  github.com/openclaw/crabbox/internal/providers/aws  0.5s
```

`bootstrapSSHHost` returns the rendered/explicit Tailscale hostname when
Tailscale is enabled, and keeps the public IP when Tailscale is disabled.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** AWS warmup probes public IP under Tailscale, unusable from EC2 operators
- **Real environment tested:** local `go test` on branch fix/aws-tailscale-bootstrap-probe (no live AWS lease in this session)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `go test ./internal/providers/aws/ -run TestBootstrapSSHHost`
- **Evidence after fix:** unit proof of host selection; source change on acquire + resolve paths
- **Observed result after fix:** Tailscale-enabled configs select hostname, disabled keep public IP
- **What was not tested:** live `crabbox warmup --network tailscale` from an EC2 operator (requires AWS + Tailscale auth)

## Summary

- When `Tailscale.Enabled`, use rendered/explicit Tailscale hostname for bootstrap SSH host
- Apply on acquire and resolve (instance id + alias)
- Unit coverage for host selection

Closes #1049

target.title: feat: add private AWS workspace service
target.body:
## Summary

- add a private, SSM-only AWS workspace path that uses the AWS SDK default credential chain and fails closed on account, Region, ECS task-role identity, and permissions
- enforce allowlisted small instance classes, encrypted configurable gp3 storage, private-subnet placement, no public address or SSH, IMDSv2, bounded networking, exact tags, lifecycle evidence, and idempotent cleanup
- add a dedicated internal ALB/ECS/PostgreSQL coordinator stack with separate execution, task, and workspace roles
- document the client URL/token contract, readiness checks, create/status/delete lifecycle, live canary, retirement procedure, and source-blind behavior contract

## Why

The portable AWS path assumes static credentials and large default workspace resources. A dedicated-account deployment needs renewable task-role credentials, strict placement checks, smaller cost-bounded workspaces, and an isolated controller that does not depend on a reusable shared control plane.

## Security and operating boundary

- the dedicated deployment rejects static AWS access keys and requires the expected account, Region, ECS metadata, and task-role identity before provisioning
- workspaces use a private subnet, no public IPv4/IPv6 address, no key pair or inbound security-group rules, IMDSv2, SSM bootstrap, encrypted gp3 volumes, and exact ownership tags
- the stack fixes this deployment to on-demand capacity and exposes instance type and volume limits only through an explicit allowlist
- this change contains no credentials, customer-specific identifiers, deployment actions, release changes, or version/tag changes
- authenticated AWS lifecycle proof remains a separate pre-merge gate; this PR must stay unmerged until create, ready/status, logs/evidence, and idempotent delete are proven in the target account

## Verification

Validated at exact head `1f87ad7bd9cec728225d8d4045f09a8163a82a86`:

- `go build -trimpath -o bin/crabbox ./cmd/crabbox`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `scripts/test-go-modules.sh`
- `scripts/check-go-coverage.sh 90.0`
- `scripts/test-provider-lifecycles.sh`
- `npm run format:check --prefix worker`
- `npm run lint --prefix worker`
- `npm run check --prefix worker`
- `npm run check:node --prefix worker`
- `npm test --prefix worker` (1,014 passed; 3 skipped)
- `npm run build --prefix worker`
- `npm run build:cloudflare-dynamic-workers --prefix worker`
- `npm run build:node --prefix worker`
- `node scripts/check-docker-base-images.mjs`
- `node --test scripts/*.test.js`
- `scripts/check-docs.sh`
- `uvx cfn-lint deploy/aws/ecs-fargate-coordinator.yaml`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --self-test`
- canonical structured autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings

## Live acceptance still required

Follow `docs/features/aws-private-workspaces.md` in an authenticated dedicated account to prove the fail-closed preflight, readiness endpoint, one create/status/delete canary, SSM and coordinator evidence, posture checks, and repeat-delete cleanup. No live cloud action is performed by this PR.

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The write tool always overwrites files. An `append: true` parameter lets the agent add content to the end of an existing file instead of replacing it. The agent requested this capability repeatedly in real sessions — it wants to write logs, build up checklists incrementally, and extend existing scripts without re-reading them first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-tool silent data loss (#40001) can happen when an agent writes to a file it has already edited without re-reading the current content. An append mode gives the agent a safer option: it can add new content without risking the loss of previous edits.

## What Changed

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to the schema, `WriteOperations.appendFile` method, append branch in `execute`, append-aware recovery (`isRecoveredAppendContent`), and post-mutation abort check matching `edit.ts:460-463`.
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to `WriteToolInput`.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — wire `appendFile` for host (`fs.appendFile`), workspace (`root.append()`), and sandbox (read-modify-write, since the sandbox bridge has no native append).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 7 new tests covering: basic append, append-to-new-file, no-op short-circuit for overwrite, malformed append param rejection, append-identical-content preserving duplicates, append-after-abort recovery via readback, and abort-surfaced-when-append-did-not-persist.

## User Impact

- `append: true` is opt-in. The default write behavior is unchanged.
- Append to a non-existent file creates it (matching `>>` shell semantics).
- The write tool description and prompt snippet advertise the new parameter.

## Evidence

Focused suite (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Tests cover: basic append, append-to-new, no-op detection for identical overwrite, malformed `append` param rejection, append identical content (duplicate tail preserved), reject append when the custom backend omits `appendFile`, post-mutation abort recovery for append (readback confirms content landed), and abort surfaced when appendFile returned without persisting.
